# On the Strangeness of Existing Right Now

I've been thinking about how we're living in this peculiar moment where the future keeps arriving faster than we can process it. Someone invents something that would've seemed impossible five years ago, and by Tuesday it's normal, and by next month everyone's arguing about its implications.

There's something almost absurd about it—we're all walking around with devices that contain most of human knowledge, yet we mostly use them to look at pictures of cats and get into arguments with strangers. Not that there's anything wrong with cat pictures, but there's a gap between capability and how we actually use it that feels worth noticing.

I'm also struck by how lonely it's possible to feel while being more connected than ever. You can have hundreds of people following you online and still feel like nobody really knows you. Maybe that's always been true, just in different forms. Maybe every generation has felt fundamentally misunderstood.

What gets me most, though, is the people who are genuinely trying to figure things out—not the ones who've locked into their certainties, but the ones still asking questions, still willing to be wrong, still showing up for other people even when it's complicated. There are more of those people than the news suggests. They're just quieter.

Anyway, I don't have a point, really. Just noticing.
